facts.fact: Spending $200,000 on broadcast TV in a competitive congressional race reaches hundreds of thousands of voters who live outside the district, according to the page's illustrative example.
facts.quote: Spend $200,000 on broadcast TV in a competitive congressional race and you're paying to reach hundreds of thousands of voters who live outside your district and can't vote for you.

facts.fact: The page claims that buying a broadcast spot in the Chicago DMA reaches eight congressional districts at once, and that 87% of impressions land on people who cannot vote for a candidate running in only one of them.
facts.quote: Buying a broadcast spot in the Chicago DMA reaches eight congressional districts at once. If you're running in just one of them, 87% of your impressions are landing on people who can't vote for you.

facts.fact: The page states that in 2024 Nielsen reported streaming overtook cable and broadcast combined for the first time.
facts.quote: In 2024, Nielsen reported that streaming overtook cable and broadcast combined for the first time.

facts.fact: The page states CTV creative can be refreshed in 24-48 hours, while a broadcast spot locked into a station's traffic system can take 5-10 days to swap.
facts.quote: A broadcast spot locked into a station's traffic system can take 5-10 days to swap. CTV creative can be refreshed in 24-48 hours

facts.fact: The page recommends that CTV represent 45-60% of total media spend in Phase 1 (June through Labor Day).
facts.quote: Recommended CTV spend share of total media: 45-60% in this phase.

facts.fact: The page recommends that CTV represent 55-65% of spend in Phase 2 (Labor Day through mid-October).
facts.quote: Recommended CTV spend share: 55-65% in this phase.

facts.fact: The page recommends that CTV represent 60-75% of spend in Phase 3 (mid-October through Election Day).
facts.quote: Recommended CTV spend share: 60-75% in this phase, with broadcast filling in the closing-week reach gaps.

facts.fact: The page suggests a frequency cap of 6-8 impressions per voter per week for CTV campaigns.
facts.quote: A frequency cap of 6-8 per voter per week prevents the campaign from saturating its highest-engagement households

facts.fact: The page describes a 4-7 p.m. weekday CTV daypart as a reach window at dinner-prep time that is less expensive per impression than network primetime.
facts.quote: A campaign running 4-7 p.m. weekday CTV spots reaches voters at dinner-prep time, before they're scrolling phones in bed, for substantially less per impression than network primetime.

facts.fact: The page states that a typical congressional district overlaps with one to four DMAs.
facts.quote: A typical congressional district overlaps with one to four DMAs, often dominated by major-metro signals that bleed across multiple districts.

facts.fact: The page states that FCC rules require equal time for opposing candidates, creating broadcast inventory bottlenecks in competitive districts.
facts.quote: Federal Communications Commission rules require equal time for opposing candidates, which creates inventory bottlenecks in competitive districts.

facts.fact: Adwave's standardized CTV ad format is 30 seconds.
facts.quote: Adwave's standardized 30-second format aligns with the platform's reality.

facts.fact: The page recommends that the first 5 seconds of a congressional CTV spot establish relevance to the viewer.
facts.quote: The first 5 seconds need to establish "this is about something I care about" or they'll mentally check out.

facts.fact: Reweighting CTV geographic allocation takes about 10 minutes per weekly adjustment, according to the page.
facts.quote: Reweighting takes 10 minutes; the impact compounds over the final month.

facts.fact: For an open-seat House race with a $4-7M cycle budget, the page estimates CTV represents $1.5M-$3M, or 30-45% of media budget.
facts.quote: Open seat with $4-7M cycle budget:** CTV typically represents $1.5M-$3M, or 30-45% of the media budget.

facts.fact: For an incumbent in a safe-but-active seat with a $2-4M cycle budget, the page estimates CTV at $600K-$1.5M, or 30-40% of media spend.
facts.quote: Incumbent in safe-but-active seat with $2-4M cycle budget:** CTV often represents $600K-$1.5M, or 30-40% of media spend.

facts.fact: For a competitive challenger with an $800K-$2M cycle budget, the page estimates CTV at 45-60% of media spend.
facts.quote: CTV is frequently the largest single channel, often 45-60% of media spend

facts.fact: For a long-shot challenger under $500K, the page estimates CTV at 60-80% of media spend.
facts.quote: Long-shot challenger under $500K:** CTV can be 60-80% of media spend

facts.fact: Competitive 2024 House campaigns reportedly had CTV costs per persuaded voter in the $15-45 range.
facts.quote: Competitive 2024 House campaigns reported CTV costs per persuaded voter in the $15-45 range

facts.fact: The page states broadcast's typical cost per persuaded voter is $80-150.
facts.quote: dramatically below broadcast's typical $80-150 range.

facts.fact: The page advises planning for 10-15% CPM growth over 2024 levels in the most competitive 30 districts.
facts.quote: Plan for 10-15% CPM growth over 2024 levels in the most competitive 30 districts.

facts.fact: The page advises campaigns to book key CTV inventory windows by mid-September.
facts.quote: Campaigns should book key inventory windows by mid-September

facts.fact: The page says the earliest meaningful CTV start for open seats and challenger races is typically June of the election year.
facts.quote: For open seats and challenger races, June of the election year is typically the earliest meaningful start.

facts.fact: The page states that Adwave is currently optimized for small business advertisers rather than political campaigns.
facts.quote: Adwave is currently optimized for small business advertisers rather than political campaigns.

facts.fact: The page states that Lowest unit charge typically does not apply on most pure-streaming CTV inventory.
facts.quote: Lowest unit charge** does not apply on most pure-streaming CTV inventory

facts.fact: The page states that the standard 'paid for by' disclosure must appear in the final seconds of a congressional CTV spot in legible text.
facts.quote: The standard "paid for by" disclosure must appear in the final seconds of the spot in legible text.

facts.fact: The page says campaigns should consider up to three separate spots, each with one message, rather than combining bio, contrast, and issue in one spot.
facts.quote: The winning campaigns run three separate spots, each doing one job

facts.fact: For competitive 2026 House races, a CTV share of 55-70% of TV spend with broadcast at 30-45% is described as increasingly common.
facts.quote: For competitive 2026 House races, CTV at 55-70% of TV spend and broadcast at 30-45% is increasingly common.

facts.fact: The page states that older, rural districts tend to skew more toward broadcast, while younger, suburban districts skew more toward CTV, when setting the CTV-to-broadcast split.
facts.quote: older, rural districts skew more broadcast; younger, suburban districts skew more CTV

facts.fact: Federal disclosure rules require the "paid for by" disclaimer to appear visually in the final seconds of a TV spot, legible at standard viewing distance.
facts.quote: Federal disclosure rules require the "paid for by" disclaimer to appear visually in the final seconds of the spot, with the disclosure legible at standard viewing distance.
